links.outcome: Calibration of FRAX predictions in positive-VFA patients before vs after local recalibration multipliers
links.effect: Multipliers derived in development cohort gave validation calibration ratios of 0.96 (MOF) and 0.90 (hip); Brier scores in positive VFA fell from 0.132 to 0.074 (MOF) and 0.043 to 0.008 (hip).
links.quote: When the recalibration multipliers were applied to the FRAX-predicted MOF and hip fracture probabilities in the validation cohort, the observed calibration ratios were 0.96 (95% CI, 0.76-1.16) and 0.90 (95% CI, 0.58-1.22), respectively ( Figure 3 ).

links.outcome: FRAX calibration in patient subgroups defined by VFA result and prior fracture
links.effect: FRAX underestimated risk in positive-VFA subgroups: with prior fracture MOF underestimated by 53% (multiplier 1.53) and hip by 76% (1.76); well calibrated in negative-VFA subgroups.
links.quote: In these individuals, FRAX underestimated MOF risk by 53% (recalibration multiplier: 1.53) and hip fracture risk by 76% (recalibration multiplier: 1.76).
